observations: Prediction gives price sixteen cents and keenest user's standalone value ten cents; launch from zero stayed at zero.
Twenty-cent standalone preset auto-launched and reached eighty-five percent with no tipping threshold.
Zero standalone value also stayed at zero, with tipping threshold twenty percent versus 7.3 percent at ten cents.
Screenshot overlays value curves and price line. Reveal explains positive standalone value can lower critical mass without eliminating the zero-start trap.

complexity.reason: Value depends on adoption share and marginal-user type.
complexity.conceptualDemand: Separate easier growth from spontaneous launch.

whyCool: Adding solo value can make a network easier to grow without giving its first user a reason to join.
caveat: Exact thresholds and uptake depend on an unspecified toy value curve; not an empirical launch forecast.
effort: Prediction, zero-start launch, all three standalone presets, overlay screenshot and reveal.
bucketReason: Clear nontrivial threshold counterexample with practical conditional insight.

prediction.evidence: Keenest initial value ten below price sixteen.

interaction.evidence: Zero, ten and twenty cents; zero versus eighty-five percent adoption.

payoff.evidence: Critical mass twenty to 7.3 percent; trap removed only when standalone value exceeds price.

clarity.evidence: Eighty-five-percent outcome and value-curve shape supplied without model equation.

surprise.evidence: Ten cents lowers threshold but adoption remains zero.
